rows.vgi.doc_llm:
## `max_flow`

Compute the **maximum flow** that can be pushed from `source` to `sink` over a capacitated network (the max-flow / min-cut value).

**Inputs.** `arcs` = `[from, to, capacity]` integer arcs; `source` and `sink` node ids. **Outputs.** One row per arc with positive flow: `from`, `to`, `flow`, `status`. Use the scalar `max_flow_value(arcs, source, sink)` when you only need the total.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
# max_flow

Maximum flow from `source` to `sink` over a capacitated network.

**Reference:** [OR-Tools documentation](https://developers.google.com/optimization/flow/maxflow)

rows.vgi.doc_llm:
## `max_flow_value`

Return the **scalar maximum-flow value** from `source` to `sink` over a capacitated network, one value per input row. `arcs` is a `LIST<LIST<BIGINT>>` of `[from, to, capacity]` triples (build it with `array_agg([f, t, cap])`); `source` and `sink` are node ids. Use the `max_flow` table function for the per-arc flow.

rows: Minimum-cost flow: route supply to demand over a capacitated, costed network at minimum total cost. Backed by OR-Tools SimpleMinCostFlow. Returns one row per arc with positive flow.

rows.vgi.doc_llm:
## `min_cost_flow`

Route flow from supply nodes to demand nodes over a **capacitated, costed network** so that total cost is minimized. Classic transportation / logistics optimization.

**Inputs.** `arcs` = `[from, to, capacity, unit_cost]` integer arcs; `supplies` = `[node, supply]` (positive at sources, negative at sinks; the supplies **must sum to zero**). All values are integers.

**Outputs.** One row per arc that carries positive flow: `from`, `to`, `flow`, `cost`, `status`. An infeasible instance returns a single `status='INFEASIBLE'` row.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
# min_cost_flow

Minimum-cost flow over a capacitated, costed network.

Supplies must sum to zero. Returns one row per arc with positive flow.

**Reference:** [OR-Tools documentation](https://developers.google.com/optimization/flow/mincostflow)

rows: Linear sum assignment: match workers to tasks over sparse [worker, task, cost] arcs, minimizing (or maximizing) total cost. Backed by OR-Tools SimpleLinearSumAssignment.

rows.vgi.doc_llm:
## `solve_assignment`

Solve a **linear sum assignment**: match each worker to at most one task (and each task to at most one worker) so the **total arc cost is minimized** (or maximized).

**Inputs.** `cost` is a sparse `LIST<LIST<BIGINT>>` of `[worker, task, cost]` integer triples (build it with `array_agg([w, t, c])`); a pair that is absent is a disallowed assignment. `maximize := true` negates costs internally. All costs must be integers.

**Outputs.** One row per matched worker: `worker`, `task`, `cost`, `status`. When no perfect matching of every worker exists the result is **exactly one row** with `status = 'INFEASIBLE'` and NULL `task`/`cost` -- never an empty set.

**Edge cases.** A non-integer cost raises a clear error (scale to integers first).
rows.vgi.doc_md:
# solve_assignment

Minimum- (or maximum-) cost matching of workers to tasks over sparse `[worker, task, cost]` arcs.

Returns one row per matched worker; an unmatchable instance returns a single `status = 'INFEASIBLE'` row.

**Reference:** [OR-Tools documentation](https://developers.google.com/optimization/assignment/linear_assignment)
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "Assign 3 workers to 3 tasks minimizing total cost (unique optimum 0->1, 1->0, 2->2).", "sql": "SELECT worker, task, cost FROM ortools.main.solve_assignment(cost := [[0,0,90],[0,1,76],[0,2,75],[1,0,35],[1,1,85],[1,2,55],[2,0,125],[2,1,95],[2,2,90]]::BIGINT[][], maximize := false) ORDER BY worker"}, {"description": "Maximize total value instead of minimizing cost.", "sql": "SELECT worker, task, cost, status FROM ortools.main.solve_assignment(cost := [[0,0,8],[0,1,7],[1,0,6],[1,1,9]]::BIGINT[][], maximize := true) ORDER BY worker"}]

1-D bin packing: assign items to the fewest identical fixed-capacity bins. CP-SAT model minimizing the number of open bins. Returns the item -> bin assignment.

rows.vgi.doc_llm:
## `solve_bin_packing`

Pack items into the **fewest identical fixed-capacity bins** (1-D bin packing as a CP-SAT model).

**Inputs.** `sizes` = `[s0, s1, ...]`; `bin_capacity` (scalar). **Outputs.** One row per item with the `bin` it is assigned to and `status`. Use `solve_bin_packing_bins(...)` for the per-bin rollup (`bin`, `used`).

Solve an arbitrary CP-SAT constraint-programming model expressed as a versioned JSON document (variables, constraints, objective). Returns one row per variable plus solve metadata. The general escape hatch for constraints highs/LP cannot express.

rows.vgi.doc_llm:
## `solve_cpsat`

Solve an **arbitrary CP-SAT constraint-programming model** handed in as a **versioned JSON document** -- the general escape hatch for everything the per-domain builders and the `highs` LP/MIP extension cannot express (global constraints like `all_different`, `no_overlap`, `cumulative`, `circuit`, reification, intervals).

**The model.** A JSON object with `version` (must be 1), `variables` (each `int` / `bool` / `interval` with a unique `name`), `constraints`, and an optional `objective`. All numeric domains are **integers** -- a fractional bound / coefficient / constant is rejected with a clear error (scale floats to integers first). The full grammar is in the README (section A).

**Outputs.** One row per variable: `var`, `value`, plus the solve metadata (`status`, `objective`, `best_bound`, `wall_time`, `num_branches`) repeated on every row so a single SELECT is self-describing. Interval variables expand to `<name>.start` / `.size` / `.end` (and `.presence` for optional intervals).

**The empty-vs-infeasible contract.** A model with no solution still returns **exactly one row** carrying `status` in {`INFEASIBLE`, `MODEL_INVALID`, `UNKNOWN`} with NULL `var`/`value`; a solve is never an empty result set. Test `WHERE status='INFEASIBLE'`, never `count(*)=0`.

**Determinism.** Single-threaded by default (`num_workers := 0`) with a fixed `random_seed`, so the objective and assignment are reproducible.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
# solve_cpsat

Solve a hand-built **CP-SAT** model expressed as a versioned JSON document.

See the README (section A) for the full JSON dialect: `variables` (int / bool / interval), `constraints` (linear, all_different, element, table, no_overlap, cumulative, circuit, reservoir, mult/div/abs/min/max equality, bool_or/and/xor, implication, with optional `enforce` reification), and an optional `objective`.

All numeric domains are integers. A no-solution model returns a single status row.

**Reference:** [OR-Tools documentation](https://developers.google.com/optimization/cp/cp_solver)
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "0/1 knapsack as a CP-SAT model: maximize value within a weight budget (optimum 40).", "sql": "SELECT var, value, status, objective FROM ortools.main.solve_cpsat(model := '{\"version\":1,\"variables\":[{\"kind\":\"bool\",\"name\":\"a\"},{\"kind\":\"bool\",\"name\":\"b\"},{\"kind\":\"bool\",\"name\":\"c\"}],\"constraints\":[{\"type\":\"linear\",\"expr\":{\"sum\":[{\"coef\":5,\"var\":\"a\"},{\"coef\":10,\"var\":\"b\"},{\"coef\":15,\"var\":\"c\"}]},\"op\":\"<=\",\"rhs\":20}],\"objective\":{\"sense\":\"maximize\",\"terms\":[{\"coef\":10,\"var\":\"a\"},{\"coef\":20,\"var\":\"b\"},{\"coef\":30,\"var\":\"c\"}]}}') ORDER BY var"}, {"description": "Single-machine no-overlap schedule minimizing makespan (optimum 10).", "sql": "SELECT objective, status FROM ortools.main.solve_cpsat(model := '{\"version\":1,\"variables\":[{\"kind\":\"int\",\"name\":\"s0\",\"lb\":0,\"ub\":20},{\"kind\":\"int\",\"name\":\"e0\",\"lb\":0,\"ub\":20},{\"kind\":\"int\",\"name\":\"s1\",\"lb\":0,\"ub\":20},{\"kind\":\"int\",\"name\":\"e1\",\"lb\":0,\"ub\":20},{\"kind\":\"int\",\"name\":\"s2\",\"lb\":0,\"ub\":20},{\"kind\":\"int\",\"name\":\"e2\",\"lb\":0,\"ub\":20},{\"kind\":\"interval\",\"name\":\"i0\",\"start\":{\"var\":\"s0\"},\"size\":{\"const\":3},\"end\":{\"var\":\"e0\"}},{\"kind\":\"interval\",\"name\":\"i1\",\"start\":{\"var\":\"s1\"},\"size\":{\"const\":5},\"end\":{\"var\":\"e1\"}},{\"kind\":\"interval\",\"name\":\"i2\",\"start\":{\"var\":\"s2\"},\"size\":{\"const\":2},\"end\":{\"var\":\"e2\"}},{\"kind\":\"int\",\"name\":\"makespan\",\"lb\":0,\"ub\":20}],\"constraints\":[{\"type\":\"no_overlap\",\"intervals\":[\"i0\",\"i1\",\"i2\"]},{\"type\":\"max_equality\",\"target\":{\"var\":\"makespan\"},\"exprs\":[{\"var\":\"e0\"},{\"var\":\"e1\"},{\"var\":\"e2\"}]}],\"objective\":{\"sense\":\"minimize\",\"terms\":[{\"coef\":1,\"var\":\"makespan\"}]}}', time_limit_s := 5.0) LIMIT 1"}]
rows.vgi.executable_examples: [{"description": "0/1 knapsack as a CP-SAT model: maximize value within a weight budget (optimum 40).", "sql": "SELECT var, value, status, objective FROM ortools.main.solve_cpsat(model := '{\"version\":1,\"variables\":[{\"kind\":\"bool\",\"name\":\"a\"},{\"kind\":\"bool\",\"name\":\"b\"},{\"kind\":\"bool\",\"name\":\"c\"}],\"constraints\":[{\"type\":\"linear\",\"expr\":{\"sum\":[{\"coef\":5,\"var\":\"a\"},{\"coef\":10,\"var\":\"b\"},{\"coef\":15,\"var\":\"c\"}]},\"op\":\"<=\",\"rhs\":20}],\"objective\":{\"sense\":\"maximize\",\"terms\":[{\"coef\":10,\"var\":\"a\"},{\"coef\":20,\"var\":\"b\"},{\"coef\":30,\"var\":\"c\"}]}}') ORDER BY var"}, {"description": "Single-machine no-overlap schedule minimizing makespan (optimum 10).", "sql": "SELECT objective, status FROM ortools.main.solve_cpsat(model := '{\"version\":1,\"variables\":[{\"kind\":\"int\",\"name\":\"s0\",\"lb\":0,\"ub\":20},{\"kind\":\"int\",\"name\":\"e0\",\"lb\":0,\"ub\":20},{\"kind\":\"int\",\"name\":\"s1\",\"lb\":0,\"ub\":20},{\"kind\":\"int\",\"name\":\"e1\",\"lb\":0,\"ub\":20},{\"kind\":\"int\",\"name\":\"s2\",\"lb\":0,\"ub\":20},{\"kind\":\"int\",\"name\":\"e2\",\"lb\":0,\"ub\":20},{\"kind\":\"interval\",\"name\":\"i0\",\"start\":{\"var\":\"s0\"},\"size\":{\"const\":3},\"end\":{\"var\":\"e0\"}},{\"kind\":\"interval\",\"name\":\"i1\",\"start\":{\"var\":\"s1\"},\"size\":{\"const\":5},\"end\":{\"var\":\"e1\"}},{\"kind\":\"interval\",\"name\":\"i2\",\"start\":{\"var\":\"s2\"},\"size\":{\"const\":2},\"end\":{\"var\":\"e2\"}},{\"kind\":\"int\",\"name\":\"makespan\",\"lb\":0,\"ub\":20}],\"constraints\":[{\"type\":\"no_overlap\",\"intervals\":[\"i0\",\"i1\",\"i2\"]},{\"type\":\"max_equality\",\"target\":{\"var\":\"makespan\"},\"exprs\":[{\"var\":\"e0\"},{\"var\":\"e1\"},{\"var\":\"e2\"}]}],\"objective\":{\"sense\":\"minimize\",\"terms\":[{\"coef\":1,\"var\":\"makespan\"}]}}', time_limit_s := 5.0) LIMIT 1"}]
rows.vgi.result_columns_schema: [{"name": "var", "type": "VARCHAR", "description": "Variable name; intervals expand to <name>.start/.size/.end/.presence."}, {"name": "value", "type": "BIGINT", "description": "Assigned integer value (NULL on a non-solution status row)."}, {"name": "status", "type": "VARCHAR", "description": "OPTIMAL/FEASIBLE/INFEASIBLE/MODEL_INVALID/UNKNOWN."}, {"name": "objective", "type": "DOUBLE", "description": "Objective value (NULL if no objective / no solution)."}, {"name": "best_bound", "type": "DOUBLE", "description": "Best objective bound (the other end of the gap)."}, {"name": "wall_time", "type": "DOUBLE", "description": "Solver wall-clock time in seconds."}, {"name": "num_branches", "type": "BIGINT", "description": "Number of search branches explored."}]

Job-shop scheduling: schedule the tasks of several jobs on shared machines (tasks of a job run in order, one task per machine at a time) to minimize the makespan. CP-SAT.

rows.vgi.doc_llm:
## `solve_jobshop`

Schedule the tasks of several **jobs** onto shared **machines** to minimize the **makespan** (the time the last task finishes). Within a job, tasks run in `task` order; each machine runs one task at a time.

**Inputs.** `tasks` = `[job, task, machine, duration]` integer rows. Optional `horizon` (defaults to the sum of durations), `time_limit_s`, `random_seed`.

**Outputs.** One row per task with its `start` / `end`, the optimal `makespan` (repeated on every row), and `status`. An infeasible / unsolved instance returns a single status row.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "Two-job, two-machine job shop minimizing makespan (optimum 7).", "sql": "SELECT job, task, machine, start, \"end\", makespan FROM ortools.main.solve_jobshop(tasks := [[0,0,0,3],[0,1,1,2],[1,0,1,2],[1,1,0,4]]::BIGINT[][], time_limit_s := 5.0) ORDER BY job, task"}]
rows.vgi.executable_examples: [{"description": "Two-job, two-machine job shop minimizing makespan (optimum 7).", "sql": "SELECT job, task, machine, start, \"end\", makespan FROM ortools.main.solve_jobshop(tasks := [[0,0,0,3],[0,1,1,2],[1,0,1,2],[1,1,0,4]]::BIGINT[][], time_limit_s := 5.0) ORDER BY job, task"}]
rows.vgi.result_columns_schema: [{"name": "job", "type": "BIGINT", "description": "Job id."}, {"name": "task", "type": "BIGINT", "description": "Task index within the job."}, {"name": "machine", "type": "BIGINT", "description": "Machine the task runs on."}, {"name": "start", "type": "BIGINT", "description": "Scheduled start time."}, {"name": "end", "type": "BIGINT", "description": "Scheduled end time (start + duration)."}, {"name": "makespan", "type": "BIGINT", "description": "Optimal makespan (repeated on every row)."}, {"name": "status", "type": "VARCHAR", "description": "OPTIMAL / FEASIBLE / INFEASIBLE / UNKNOWN."}]

Multi-dimensional 0/1 knapsack: choose items to maximize total value subject to one or more capacity dimensions. Backed by OR-Tools KnapsackSolver (branch and bound).

rows.vgi.doc_llm:
## `solve_knapsack`

Choose a subset of items to **maximize total value** subject to one or more **capacity dimensions** (multi-dimensional 0/1 knapsack).

**Inputs.** `item_values` = `[v0, v1, ...]`; `weights` = `[[w0_d0, w0_d1, ...], ...]` (one row per item, one column per capacity dimension); `capacities` = `[c_d0, c_d1, ...]`. **Outputs.** One row per item with `chosen` (`BOOLEAN`) and `status`.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "Single-dimension 0/1 knapsack: pick items maximizing value within capacity 40 (optimum 80).", "sql": "SELECT item, chosen FROM ortools.main.solve_knapsack(item_values := [10,20,30,40,50]::BIGINT[], weights := [[5],[10],[15],[20],[25]]::BIGINT[][], capacities := [40]::BIGINT[]) ORDER BY item"}, {"description": "Two-dimensional knapsack: each item has a weight and a volume, packed under both a weight budget (50) and a volume budget (5) at once -- one `weights` column per dimension.", "sql": "SELECT item, chosen, status FROM ortools.main.solve_knapsack(item_values := [60,100,120]::BIGINT[], weights := [[10,2],[20,3],[30,4]]::BIGINT[][], capacities := [50,5]::BIGINT[]) ORDER BY item"}]
rows.vgi.executable_examples: [{"description": "Single-dimension 0/1 knapsack: pick items maximizing value within capacity 40 (optimum 80).", "sql": "SELECT item, chosen FROM ortools.main.solve_knapsack(item_values := [10,20,30,40,50]::BIGINT[], weights := [[5],[10],[15],[20],[25]]::BIGINT[][], capacities := [40]::BIGINT[]) ORDER BY item"}, {"description": "Two-dimensional knapsack: each item has a weight and a volume, packed under both a weight budget (50) and a volume budget (5) at once -- one `weights` column per dimension.", "sql": "SELECT item, chosen, status FROM ortools.main.solve_knapsack(item_values := [60,100,120]::BIGINT[], weights := [[10,2],[20,3],[30,4]]::BIGINT[][], capacities := [50,5]::BIGINT[]) ORDER BY item"}]

Resource-constrained project scheduling (RCPSP): schedule tasks with durations, precedences, and per-resource capacity (renewable) to minimize makespan. CP-SAT cumulative.

rows.vgi.doc_llm:
## `solve_rcpsp`

Solve a **resource-constrained project scheduling problem**: schedule tasks (each with a duration and a per-resource demand) subject to finish-to-start **precedences** and renewable **resource capacities**, minimizing the makespan.

**Inputs.** `tasks` = `[task, duration, r0_demand, r1_demand, ...]` (one demand column per resource, in `resources` order); `precedences` = `[pred, succ]`; `resources` = `[resource, capacity]`. **Outputs.** One row per task with `start` / `end`, the optimal `makespan`, and `status`.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
# solve_rcpsp

Resource-constrained project scheduling minimizing makespan.

**Reference:** [OR-Tools documentation](https://developers.google.com/optimization/scheduling/job_shop)
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "Four-task project, one resource of capacity 2, with two precedences.", "sql": "SELECT task, start, \"end\", makespan, status FROM ortools.main.solve_rcpsp(tasks := [[0,3,2],[1,2,1],[2,4,2],[3,2,1]]::BIGINT[][], precedences := [[0,2],[1,3]]::BIGINT[][], resources := [[0,2]]::BIGINT[][], time_limit_s := 5.0) ORDER BY task"}]

Travelling salesperson: shortest single-vehicle tour visiting every node once and returning to the start, over a distance matrix. OR-Tools routing library.

rows.vgi.doc_llm:
## `solve_tsp`

Find the **shortest single-vehicle tour** that visits every node once and returns to `start`, over a distance matrix.

**Inputs.** `distance` is either sparse `[from, to, meters]` integer triples (build with `array_agg([f, t, m])`) or a dense `n x n` matrix; `start` is the depot node. **Outputs.** The tour in visit order: `seq`, `node`, `arrival` (cumulative distance), `status`. The tour rotation / direction may vary but the length is optimal.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
# solve_tsp

Shortest single-vehicle tour over a distance matrix.

**Reference:** [OR-Tools documentation](https://developers.google.com/optimization/routing/tsp)

Vehicle routing problem: route a fleet from a depot to serve stops at minimum total distance, with optional capacity dimensions, time windows, service/travel time, pickup-delivery pairs, droppable stops, and route balancing. OR-Tools routing library.

rows.vgi.doc_llm:
## `solve_vrp`

Route a **fleet of vehicles** from a depot to serve a set of stops at **minimum total distance**, with the full routing surface: multi-dimension **capacity** (`demand` + `vehicle_capacity`), **time windows** (`time_windows` + `service_time` / `travel_time`), **pickup-delivery** pairs (same vehicle + precedence), droppable stops (`allow_dropping` + `drop_penalty`), route balancing (`span_cost_coefficient`), and the OR-Tools `first_solution_strategy` / `local_search_metaheuristic`.

**Inputs.** `distance` (sparse `[from, to, meters]` or dense `n x n`); `demand` = `[node, d0, d1, ...]` (the number of demand columns sets the number of capacity dimensions and therefore the `load_0` .. `load_k` output columns); `num_vehicles`; `vehicle_capacity`; `depot`. Advanced shapes -- per-vehicle / per-dimension capacities, per-vehicle `[start, end]` depots -- go through `settings_json`.

**Outputs.** One row per stop: `route_id` (vehicle), `seq`, `node`, `arrival`, `departure`, `load_0` .. `load_k`, `is_dropped`, `status`. A dropped node appears as a single row with `is_dropped = true` and NULL `route_id`. An unsolved instance returns one status row.

**Determinism.** Governed by the fixed `first_solution_strategy` / `local_search_metaheuristic`. The output `load_*` column count is fixed at bind time from the `demand` argument, so pass `demand` as a literal or a session VARIABLE that is set before the query binds.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "Capacitated VRP: 1 depot, 3 stops of demand 1, 2 vehicles of capacity 2 (optimal distance 6).", "sql": "SELECT route_id, seq, node, arrival, load_0 FROM ortools.main.solve_vrp(distance := [[0,1,1],[0,2,1],[0,3,2],[1,0,1],[1,2,1],[1,3,2],[2,0,1],[2,1,1],[2,3,1],[3,0,2],[3,1,2],[3,2,1]]::BIGINT[][], demand := [[1,1],[2,1],[3,1]]::BIGINT[][], num_vehicles := 2, vehicle_capacity := 2, depot := 0, time_limit_s := 1.0) ORDER BY route_id, seq"}]
rows.vgi.executable_examples: [{"description": "Capacitated VRP: 1 depot, 3 stops of demand 1, 2 vehicles of capacity 2 (optimal distance 6).", "sql": "SELECT route_id, seq, node, arrival, load_0 FROM ortools.main.solve_vrp(distance := [[0,1,1],[0,2,1],[0,3,2],[1,0,1],[1,2,1],[1,3,2],[2,0,1],[2,1,1],[2,3,1],[3,0,2],[3,1,2],[3,2,1]]::BIGINT[][], demand := [[1,1],[2,1],[3,1]]::BIGINT[][], num_vehicles := 2, vehicle_capacity := 2, depot := 0, time_limit_s := 1.0) ORDER BY route_id, seq"}]
rows.vgi.keywords: ["vrp", "vehicle routing", "cvrp", "capacitated routing", "time windows", "pickup delivery", "fleet routing", "last mile", "logistics", "or-tools", "optimization"]
rows.vgi.result_dynamic_columns_md:
The number of `load_d` columns is fixed at bind time from the `demand` argument (one per capacity dimension), so the output schema varies by call. For `k+1` capacity dimensions the columns are:

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| route_id | INTEGER | Vehicle index (NULL on a dropped-node row). |
| seq | INTEGER | 0-based stop order on the vehicle. |
| node | BIGINT | Node id (depot at seq 0 and last). |
| arrival | BIGINT | Cumulative time/distance at arrival. |
| departure | BIGINT | Arrival + service time. |
| load_0 | BIGINT | Cumulative load for capacity dimension 0. |
| load_k | BIGINT | Cumulative load for capacity dimension k (one load_d column per dimension). |
| is_dropped | BOOLEAN | True on the row emitted for a dropped node. |
| status | VARCHAR | OPTIMAL / FEASIBLE / INFEASIBLE / UNKNOWN / MODEL_INVALID. |
rows.vgi.title: Vehicle Routing (Capacitated / Time-Windowed)
